# Deploy generated files

Deploys run from a local checkout; CI never deploys. Deploy only when the request asks for publication.

`scripts/deploy.py` runs this whole playbook and [Stage B](../verify-post-deploy.md) in one call and prints one TOON report: the failing items first, then every check as `stage,check,status,evidence`, the counts, the backup, and next-step hints. Its exit code is 0 for a pass, 1 for a failure and 2 for a usage or environment error. Full logs, the upload rows and the full report (with every uploaded path) go to one directory per deploy, which the output names; do not pipe them through `grep` or `tail`. Do not hand-write `ssh`, `curl`, `sha256sum` or backup commands, and do not write a separate deploy report: the tool's report is the deploy report.

1. Run [Stage A](../verify.md#stage-a-pre-deploy). Stop if it fails.
2. Resolve the destination at deploy time, never in the repository: the SSH host alias (which also supplies the user), the document root on it, and the public site URL. Give them as `--host`, `--docroot` and `--base-url`, as `SITE_DEPLOY_HOST`, `SITE_DEPLOY_DOCROOT` and `SITE_DEPLOY_BASE_URL`, or as `host`, `docroot` and `base_url` in `~/.config/teoyujie-site/deploy.toml` (or the file `SITE_DEPLOY_CONFIG` names). Backups go to `site-backups/` in the SSH user's home unless `backups` says otherwise; logs and reports go to `~/.local/state/teoyujie-site/deploys/` unless `state_dir` says otherwise. Set `VISUALS_REPO` (or `visuals_repo`) to a clean yujieteo/visuals checkout at a commit on visuals main.
3. Check out the commit the request asks for, with no uncommitted changes, and make sure it is pushed: the tool refuses a commit whose CI run (on its pull request or on `main`) has not passed.
4. Dry run: `.venv/bin/python scripts/deploy.py plan`. It checks the work tree and CI, builds the site, derives the upload set with `scripts/site_diff.py` against the site and visuals commits that are live, checks the upload set with `scripts/deploy_check.py`'s path rules, and compares the sha256 of every built file with the live document root. The live pair comes from the tool's deploy log; for the first deploy with the tool, pass it as `--base <site commit> --visuals-base <visuals commit>` (the last deploy that was recorded by hand). The plan fails when a live file outside the upload set differs from the build, because the deploy would leave it stale: pass an older `--base` (that only adds files whose bytes are already live). `--scoped-verdict` lets the verdict follow the upload set alone; use it only when the request accepts that drift, and say so in the report, which counts the files outside the scope.
5. Review the upload set in the rows file the plan names: one `A` (added), `M` (modified) or `D` (no longer generated) row per file, `corpus.json` first. The tool uploads every `A` and `M` path and leaves `D` paths on the host. The set can include large pinned downloads, such as `site/visuals/beamdswitch/kokoro/**` (about 440 MB, the largest file 326 MB); they are listed only when their pin in `visuals/<slug>/raw.json` changed since the base, or on their first deploy, and the upload takes longer.
6. Deploy: `.venv/bin/python scripts/deploy.py run --execute`. It repeats every plan check, then bundles the upload set with `COPYFILE_DISABLE=1 tar` (no AppleDouble `._*` files), unpacks it into this deploy's own `fm-deploy-` backup directory on the host, verifies its sha256 there, and installs every file in one pass, as [Atomic safe deploy](../principles/atomic-safe-deploy.md) says: a temporary sibling with mode 0644, the prior file preserved in the backup, then a rename, `corpus.json` first and `visuals/beamdswitch/coi-serviceworker.js` in the same install as `visuals/beamdswitch/index.html`. It then runs Stage B. A Stage B failure on an uploaded file restores every preserved prior file and keeps the backup; a pass removes this deploy's backup directory and nothing else. Each run appends one line to the deploy log, which the next plan reads for its base.
7. Report the tool's output as it printed it. `.venv/bin/python scripts/deploy.py report` prints the last deploy again (`--deploy <id>` for an older one), and `.venv/bin/python scripts/deploy.py backups` lists the backup directories on the host with the rollback command for any `fm-deploy-` one left by a failed run; it never removes one.

To re-run one Stage B check by hand, use the `scripts/deploy_check.py` command that [Stage B](../verify-post-deploy.md) names, with the rows file the tool saved.

Principles: [No secrets in the repository](../principles/no-secrets-in-repo.md), [Atomic safe deploy](../principles/atomic-safe-deploy.md), and [Generated files are read-only](../principles/generated-files-are-read-only.md).
